question:
A product consists of three components, which are produced by four workshops. The total number of production hours available for each workshop is limited. Table 1.4 shows the productivity of the three components. The objective is to determine how many hours should be allocated to each component in each workshop in order to maximize the number of completed products. Represent this problem as a linear programming problem. Table 1.4 | Workshop | Production Capacity
(hours) | Productivity (units/hour) | | | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | | | Component 1 | Component 2 | Component 3 | | A | 100 | 10 | 15 | 5 | | B | 150 | 15 | 10 | 5 | | C | 80 | 20 | 5 | 10 | | D | 200 | 10 | 15 | 20 |

    components = list(d["productivity"][workshops[0]].keys())

    m.C = pyo.Set(initialize=components, ordered=True)    # components 1..3

    def x_bounds(m, w, c):
        return (0, d["capacity"][w])

                  domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                  bounds=x_bounds)

    # --- Objective: maximize completed products ---
    def obj_rule(m):
        return m.P

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # --- Constraint 1: workshop capacity (hours) ---
    def cap_rule(m, w):
        return sum(m.x[w, c] for c in m.C) <= d["capacity"][w]

    m.capacity_limit = pyo.Constraint(m.W, rule=cap_rule)

    # --- Constraint 2: enough units of each component per product ---
    # total units of component c produced across all workshops >= P
    def comp_rule(m, c):
        return sum(d["productivity"][w][c] * m.x[w, c] for w in m.W) >= m.P

    m.component_balance = pyo.Constraint(m.C, rule=comp_rule)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA = {
    "workshops": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
    "components": [1, 2, 3],
    "capacity": {
        "A": 100,
        "B": 150,
        "C": 80,

    "productivity": {

        "B": {1: 15, 2: 10, 3: 5},
        "C": {1: 20, 2: 5, 3: 10},
        "D": {1: 10, 2: 15, 3: 20},
    },
    # Each completed product requires exactly one unit of each component.
    "components_per_product": 1,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    workshops = d["workshops"]
    components = d["components"]
    capacity = d["capacity"]
    productivity = d["productivity"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Sets
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    model.W = pyo.Set(initialize=workshops, ordered=True)
    model.C = pyo.Set(initialize=components, ordered=True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Decision variables
    # x[i, j] = hours allocated in workshop i to producing component j
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.W,
        model.C,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=(0, None),
    )

    # N = number of completed products (units of the final product)
    model.N = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, None))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective: maximize the number of completed products
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.N, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Constraint 1: workshop capacity limits
    #   sum_j x[i, j] <= capacity[i]   for each workshop i
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def capacity_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for j in m.C) <= capacity[i]

    model.capacity_con = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=capacity_rule)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Constraint 2: component balance
    #   Each completed product needs one unit of each component.
    #   Total units of component j produced across all workshops must be
    #   at least N (the number of completed products).
    #   sum_i productivity[i][j] * x[i, j] >= N   for each component j
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def balance_rule(m, j):
        return (
            sum(productivity[i][j] * m.x[i, j] for i in m.W)
            >= d["components_per_product"] * m.N
        )

    model.balance_con = pyo.Constraint(model.C, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Problem: allocate limited workshop hours among three components so as to
# maximise the number of completed products (each product needs 1 unit of
# each of the three components).
#
# Decision variables
#   x[w, j] : hours allocated in workshop w to component j   (>= 0, continuous)
#   P       : number of completed products assembled            (>= 0)
#
# Objective (maximise):  P
#
# Constraints
#   (1) Workshop capacity:  sum_j x[w, j] <= capacity[w]        for each w
#   (2) Component balance:  sum_w rate[w, j] * x[w, j] >= P     for each j
#       (each finished product consumes one unit of every component)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "workshops": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
    "components": [1, 2, 3],
    # production capacity in hours for each workshop
    "capacity": {"A": 100, "B": 150, "C": 80, "D": 200},
    # productivity (units per hour) of each component in each workshop
    "rate": {
        ("A", 1): 10, ("A", 2): 15, ("A", 3): 5,
        ("B", 1): 15, ("B", 2): 10, ("B", 3): 5,
        ("C", 1): 20, ("C", 2): 5,  ("C", 3): 10,
        ("D", 1): 10, ("D", 2): 15, ("D", 3): 20,
    },
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.W = pyo.Set(initialize=d["workshops"])
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=d["components"])

    # x[w, j]: hours allocated in workshop w to component j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.W, model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # P: number of completed products
    model.P = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # (1) workshop capacity constraints
    def cap_rule(m, w):
        return sum(m.x[w, j] for j in m.J) <= d["capacity"][w]

    model.capacity_con = pyo.Constraint(model.W, rule=cap_rule)

    # (2) component balance constraints: production of each component >= P
    def balance_rule(m, j):
        return sum(d["rate"][(w, j)] * m.x[w, j] for w in m.W) >= m.P

    model.balance_con = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=balance_rule)

    # objective: maximise number of completed products
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.P, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):

    workshops = d["workshops"]
    components = d["components"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=workshops, ordered=True)   # workshops
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=components, ordered=True)  # components
    model.IJ = pyo.Set(initialize=[(i, j) for i in workshops for j in components],
                       dimen=2)                             # (workshop, component) pairs

    # Variables
    # x[i,j]: hours allocated in workshop i to component j (>= 0, continuous)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.IJ, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # n: number of completed products (>= 0, continuous)

    # Capacity constraint: hours used in a workshop cannot exceed its capacity (<=)
    def capacity_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for j in m.J) <= d["capacity"][i]
    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=capacity_rule)

    # Product assembly: n cannot exceed units of any single component produced (<=)
    def assembly_rule(m, j):
        return m.n <= sum(d["productivity"][(i, j)] * m.x[i, j] for i in m.I)
    model.assembly = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=assembly_rule)

    # Objective: maximise the number of completed products
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.n, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model
